## Summary

Built a new `orders` module following sheratan's canonical shape, wired as the app's composition root:

- **`services/orders.contract.ts`** — `Order`, `OrderStatus`, `OrdersApi` interface.
- **`services/orders.http.ts`** — HTTP adapter hitting `/api/orders` and `PATCH /api/orders/:id`, extracting the server's `{error}` message on failure.
- **`modules/orders/orders.state.ts`** — signals/transitions; `shipStarted`/`shipRolledBack` carry the pre-optimistic order snapshot so rollback restores the exact prior status (not just a boolean).
- **`modules/orders/orders.effects.ts`** — `resource()` loads the list with retry; `mutation()` drives the ship write with `optimistic`/`rollback` wired to state, keyed by order id so concurrent ships on different rows don't block each other; on failure, shows a toast with the server's message.
- **`modules/orders/orders.view.ts`** — renders rows (`data-testid="order-row"`), status badge (`data-testid="status"`), and Mark Shipped button (`data-testid="ship"`, disabled while in flight or already shipped), plus a dismissible toast (`data-testid="toast"`).
- Updated `app.ts` and `styles/global.css` to mount the module.

Verified: `tsc`, `oxlint`, `sheratan check` (no violations), and all 33 unit tests pass. Also drove it in a real headless browser against the running server — confirmed the optimistic badge update, successful settle, and (via a mocked 409) the rollback-to-previous-status plus toast with the exact server error text.
